first_impression: My immediate reaction is that this looks surprisingly warm, focused, and well-designed, like a cozy cross between Untitled Goose Game and an actual sheepdog trial. The graphic design of the menus is gorgeous, though the in-game 3D world looks slightly sparse and low-poly prototype-tier. Still, herding sheep as a border collie with creeping and barking mechanics immediately sells the fantasy.
best_things: The UI presentation and typographic style are immaculate, giving the entire game a rich, authentic Scottish pastoral feel.
Instead of just increasing sheep counts, every level injects distinct mechanical twists like stubborn rams, storms flooding crossings, and night defense.
The influence ring and creep mechanic give clear, readable feedback on how your physical presence impacts flock panic levels.

worst_problems.problem: Narrow chokepoints like wooden bridges look primed for frustrating AI pathfinding snags where sheep get stuck on railing corners.
worst_problems.suggestion: Add flock funneling guidance along bridge ramps so sheep don't awkwardly bundle against railings or slide off edges.

worst_problems.problem: The dog model and creeping posture look stiff and slightly disconnected from the ground plane.
worst_problems.suggestion: Give Pip smoother spine flexing and lower-to-the-ground stalking animations so he feels like an agile predator rather than a sliding low-poly mesh.

worst_problems.problem: The environment across large fields is noticeably empty, consisting mostly of flat green plains and identical scattered rocks.
worst_problems.suggestion: Add varied ground clutter like heather patches, muddy tractor ruts, stone dykes, and variable grass heights to break up the flat geometry.

worst_problems.problem: Night Watch mode abruptly swaps the relaxing herding loop for anxious radar-watching perimeter defense.
worst_problems.suggestion: Provide more proactive tools to deter wolves during the night, like marking territory or herding sheep into natural shelter, rather than reactive frantic sprinting.

worst_problems.problem: Level intro and result overlays look like modern web modal dialogues rather than feeling integrated into the world.
worst_problems.suggestion: Skin the UI containers to look like a shepherd's field notebook or parchment to match the rustic aesthetic.

boredom_points: Slowly inching behind a stubborn single sheep across a massive open pasture when creeping to avoid spooking it.
Waiting for the countdown clock in Night Watch once your flock is already pinned against a map boundary.
confusions: It is unclear whether sheep that bump against water or bridge edges will drown or if water has an invisible wall.
The wolf interaction rules aren't totally obvious - can Pip take damage or get killed, or do wolves only target sheep?
wish_list: A shepherd character whistling audio cues to direct you across the hills.
More fluid, liquid flocking algorithms so larger herds split and regroup naturally like real sheep.
A free-roam endless evening mode where you can just practice herding across the valley without a timer.
one_line_review: A surprisingly smart, cozy sheepdog puzzle game that turns Highland herding into a tight seasonal campaign, even if the low-poly world feels a bit stiff.
